html:
SMTO-SKL-0013 — Your Google account hasn't allowed this Calendar access yet

GUID: 9d636142-e99c-5471-95fc-2b35b242d8e3
Slug: google-calendar-scope-missing
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • Your Google account is connected, but it hasn't given SMTO permission for this kind of Calendar task, such as editing events. The task was stopped, so your calendar wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to reconnect your Google account for Calendar with the access this task needs, and open the Google link it gives you. The account was approved for less than this task needs, and only a new Google approval can add more.
  2. On Google's page, sign in with the same account as before and allow every Calendar permission it lists. Approving with a different account or skipping a permission leaves the original account still missing access.
  3. Ask SMTO to check the Google account's connection status, then ask for the calendar task again. The status shows whether the needed Calendar access is now granted, so the next try won't fail the same way.

What success looks like

  • The connection status lists the needed Calendar access and SMTO completes the task.

If it still fails

  • Your organization's Google administrator may block this access for outside apps. Select Copy error details and send them to that administrator or the person who manages SMTO. Don't connect a different Google account to get around it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected google_account lacks the OAuth scopes for the Calendar feature this operation needs (local feature check or Google insufficientPermissions/insufficientAuthenticationScopes), so a consent upgrade is required.

What this means

  • Google reports insufficient OAuth permissions/scopes or local shared-account feature checks require a consent upgrade. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google reports insufficient OAuth permissions/scopes or local shared-account feature checks require a consent upgrade.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect required/missing features and provider reason separately from calendar sharing permissions.

How to fix it

  • Run auth.google_connect or google_calendar.connect with the same auth_app_ref and account_key and the missing_features from the error details (for example calendar_write or calendar_list), complete consent as the same Google identity, then confirm with google_calendar.connection_status. Check that the google_oauth_app record and the Workspace admin's API controls allow those scopes.
  • Use auth.google_connect or google_calendar.connect with the same OAuth app and account_key and the reported required_features or missing_features. Then inspect google_calendar.connection_status.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use auth.google_connect or google_calendar.connect with the same OAuth app and account_key and the reported required_features or missing_features. Then inspect google_calendar.connection_status.

How to verify the fix

  • The same intended account grants the explicit required feature and connection status confirms it.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
